It operates within a Public Land Mobile Network (PLMN) and can be accessed by other instances of 5G PKMF in different PLMNs, enabling inter-PLMN key management and service coordination. The function provides critical services including key request handling, remote user ID resolution, and discovery operations, supporting both Request/Response and event-driven interactions.

5G PKMF plays a central role in enabling secure and authorized discovery and communication among User Equipment (UE) in proximity-based scenarios. It manages and delivers discovery keys for use in Model B restricted discovery, supporting operations such as announcing, monitoring, and enabling restricted discovery for discoverer UEs. It also provides authorization services for announcements and manages the creation or update of resource contexts based on userInfoId, ensuring secure and context-aware service delivery.

Application enablement architecture is a technical framework studied in the present document for supporting mobile metaverse services over 3GPP networks. 3GPP networks are the underlying telecommunications infrastructure over which mobile metaverse services are enabled, and on which the application enablement architecture is studied.

Architectural requirements are defined as part of the study to guide the design of the application enablement architecture for mobile metaverse services.

Related use cases are defined in 3GPP TR 22.856 [3] and are considered in the study to inform the development of the application enablement architecture for mobile metaverse services.
Corresponding solutions are developed as part of the study to support the application layer functional model and provide enablement layer support to metaverse applications.

Measurement result characteristics define the attributes and behavior of measurement results produced by a measurement job during specified recording intervals. Results are generated at the end of the granularity period if the job is not suspended, and all results for a single measurement job are aggregated into one report. Performance Alarms are a type of alarm that enables Network Operators to be quickly informed of significant PM-related events. They are triggered when measurement thresholds are either crossed or reached, and authorized users can set thresholds and define notification characteristics such as perceivedSeverity. The source object of the alarm is the instance of the measurement that caused the alarm. Subscribed users, known as Notification IRP Managers, are notified via the Alarm IRP and Notification IRP. Performance Alarms may be defined on any managed object supporting measurement definitions, such as UtranCell or SgsnFunction. Once raised, they are managed like other alarms (e.g., acknowledged, unacknowledged, annotated) and cannot be manually cleared via ADMC. Instead, they are cleared when the threshold is crossed or reached in the opposite direction to the triggering event.

Notification IRP is a protocol used in conjunction with the Alarm IRP to deliver performance alarm notifications to subscribed users, specifically Notification IRP Managers. It is described in TS 32.302 [11] and is involved in the notification process triggered by threshold crossing or reaching.

PM application is the user of the Alarm IRP that provides the alarm notification parameters, including event type, probable cause, perceived severity, thresholdinfo, and other mandatory user-supplied parameters. It is responsible for supplying the context-specific data required for performance alarm notifications.

A trust domain is a network segment or administrative boundary within which functional entities are mutually trusted to exchange messages under a shared security and trust policy. It serves as a defined region where entities are considered trustworthy and can communicate with specific header fields—such as P-Asserted-Identity (per RFC 3325), Resource-Priority, Reason, and Privacy—preserved and properly managed. The Binding Support Function (BSF) is a network function that stores internal information about selected PCFs for PDU Sessions and UEs. For a PDU Session, it stores user identity, DNN, UE IP or MAC address, S-NSSAI, selected PCF address, and optionally PCF instance ID, PCF set ID, and level of binding. For a UE, it stores user identity, selected PCF address, and optionally PCF instance ID, PCF set ID, and level of binding. The BSF supports only NF instance or NF set level of binding. It verifies and provides PCF addresses based on input from consumer NFs such as AF, NEF, or PCF for the UE. 3GPP Release 19 (Rel-19) is the second release of 5G-Advanced and the last release fully dedicated to 5G. Stage 3/RAN freeze was September 2025, RAN4 March 2026. Rel-19 consists almost exclusively of improvements to features introduced in earlier releases, plus one new feature: Ambient power-enabled IoT. It also serves as a bridge to 6G by hosting two 6G-oriented channel-modeling studies (ISAC and 7-24 GHz).

Non-Terrestrial Networks for NR Phase 3 continues the Rel-17/Rel-18 NTN evolution. It improves NR downlink coverage in NTN via repetitions of PDCCH in the common search space, repetitions of PDSCH carrying Msg4 and SIB1, and extended SS/PBCH block periodicity up to 160 ms. Uplink capacity is improved via inter-slot orthogonal cover codes for PUSCH. Multicast/broadcast service support is added when the satellite service area is smaller than the Uu cell coverage area. Regenerative payload architectures with a full gNB on board the satellite are supported, and RedCap / enhanced RedCap operation is added in FR1 NR-NTN bands.

Satellite access Phase 3 introduces five new capabilities: Store-and-Forward (S&F) satellite operation, UE-Satellite-UE direct communication, GNSS-independent operation, positioning enhancements for satellite access, and LAN/service improvements over satellite. Work spans SA1 (requirements), SA2 (architecture, results in TR 23.700-29), SA3 (security), SA5 (charging), SA6 (application enablement, mission critical), CT1/CT3/CT4 (stage 3 protocol enhancements), and RAN2/RAN3 (NTN). Normative service requirements are added to TS 22.261; the requirements related to satellite access are consolidated into one dedicated section to ease future stage-2 and stage-3 work.

NTN for IoT Phase 3 introduces Store-and-Forward satellite operation using a full eNB as a regenerative payload, uplink capacity improvements via orthogonal cover codes for NPUSCH, and broadcast support for public warning system (PWS) messages over NB-IoT. A new barring mechanism distinguishes S&F-capable UEs from legacy ones, allowing S&F-capable devices to be served while legacy devices are barred. New system information indicates S&F mode and transition timing. Uplink capacity gains come from OCC support on NPUSCH format 1, with slot-level OCC for 15 kHz SCS and symbol-level OCC for 3.75 kHz SCS, plus OCC-based reference signals. Diversity slotted ALOHA is supported for Msg3.

A regenerative satellite payload hosts a full 3GPP gNB or eNB on board the satellite, as opposed to a transparent payload that simply relays the radio signal. Regenerative payloads enable Store-and-Forward operation, regenerative multi-satellite routing, and integration of RAN and CN functions inside the satellite. Rel-19 introduces regenerative payload support as part of NTN Ph3 and 5GSAT Ph3, including architectural studies in TR 23.700-29.

RedCap (Reduced Capability NR) support in FR1 NR-NTN bands. Rel-19 adds RedCap and enhanced RedCap device operation in NTN bands so low-complexity NR devices can connect via satellite while keeping their reduced-capability profile.

The Rel-19 satellite cluster, comprising NTN for NR Phase 3, Satellite Access Phase 3, NTN for IoT Phase 3 (LTE), UAS, Aerial, and Regenerative Payload. 5GSAT was introduced in Rel-17; Rel-19 is its Phase 3 of independent improvements.

Ambient power-enabled IoT (AmbientIoT or A-IoT) is the single brand-new Rel-19 feature. It targets ultra-low-power, ultra-simple IoT devices that harvest energy from the ambient environment (RF backscatter, active transmissions at low power, energy harvesting). Two topologies are considered: a base station connected directly to a tag, and a UE serving as an intermediate node under network control. Work is split between SA/CT (service requirements and stage 3) and RAN (Solutions for Ambient IoT in NR). Frequency range is FR1 FDD.

Rel-19 IoT and RedCap improvements include power class 2 RedCap UE operation in NR FR1, NAS-layer overhead reduction for data transfer over Control Plane CIoT, and management aspects of RedCap features. Rel-19 also continues the work on LTE-based IoT optimizations from Rel-10 onwards.

Rel-19 specifies a normative framework for one-sided AI/ML models at the gNB or UE, covering beam management, positioning, and CSI prediction. A generic lifecycle-management framework is defined. Detailed use-case enhancements include beam prediction in the spatial and temporal domains, positioning prediction, and CSI prediction. Two-sided CSI compression and UE training-data collection are deferred to Rel-20. AI/ML for mobility management is studied in RAN2.

Rel-19 enhances Rel-18's AI/ML-based NG-RAN architecture work with candidate topics: split architecture support, mobility optimization for NR dual connectivity, multi-hop UE trajectory across gNBs, energy cost prediction, continuous MDT collection across RRC states, AI/ML-based network slicing, and coverage/capacity optimization (cell shaping).

Rel-19 second phase of AI/ML management: signaling and protocols essential to the Lifecycle Management (LCM) of AI/ML models, including training, training-data collection, model input/output design, performance monitoring, and enabling/disabling/switching of models. Charging aspects of Ambient AI/ML are also defined.

Rel-19 AI/ML cluster comprising AI/ML for NR air interface, AI/ML for NG-RAN enhancements, AI/ML Management Phase 2, AI/ML for mobility (RAN2 study), AI/ML for energy management, AI/ML data collection from UPF, and RAN4 performance requirements for AI/ML in the RAN.

Rel-19 enhancements of NR network energy savings. Building on the Rel-18 study, Rel-19 specifies further mechanisms for the gNB and UE to reduce power consumption, including more aggressive always-off signal patterns, cell DTX/DRX extensions, and AI/ML-based energy saving.

Rel-19 specifies a low-power wake-up signal (LP-WUS) and a corresponding low-power wake-up receiver (LP-WUR) at the UE. The LP-WUR monitors a wake-up signal that is much cheaper to decode than the full NR PDCCH; when detected, the main NR receiver is powered up. This dramatically reduces UE power consumption during idle and inactive states. Based on the Rel-18 LP-WUS study.
Rel-19 energy-efficiency cluster: Network Energy Savings for NR, LP-WUS/WUR for NR, Energy Efficiency as Service Criteria, and AI/ML-based energy management.

Rel-19 enhancements of 3GPP Northbound and Application Layer Interfaces and APIs, Service Enabler Architecture, NPN considerations, security for PLMN hosting an NPN, SNPN interconnection, and ProSe support in NPN.
ProSe (Proximity Services) support for SNPN and PNI-NPN, including discovery and communication among UEs authorized for the same NPN. Specified in TS 23.304 and related 24/33-series specs.

Non-Public Networks (NPN) are private 5G networks for enterprises, factories, and other verticals. There are two types: SNPN (Standalone NPN, identified by a PLMN ID and NID pair) and PNI-NPN (Public Network Integrated NPN, a slice of a public PLMN). Rel-19 enhances both with security improvements, SNPN interconnection, and ProSe support.
Rel-19 Phase 2 of the system architecture for Next Generation Real-time Communication services, including security support and application enablement aspects for MMTel.

Rel-19 Phase 2/3 of XR, AR, Metaverse, and Edge Computing. Includes Localized Mobile Metaverse services, XR media, split rendering over IMS, Edge Computing Phase 3, Edge Computing for Industrial Scenarios, and Edge Computing Considering Operational Needs of Service Hosting Environment.

Rel-19 defines high-power UE operation (power class 1.5 or 2) for NR intra-band CA, NR inter-band CA/DC combinations with/without UL, NR FR1 TDD/FDD single band, and high-power UE operation (power class 2) for FWA use cases in a single LTE band. HPUE allows UEs to transmit at higher power for fixed-wireless access and similar scenarios where link budget is critical.

Rel-19 5G NR Femto enables plug-and-play deployment of small indoor NR access nodes with controlled user access. Enhanced via NEF/UDM support for CAG information and flexible deployment options (including optional Femto GW and local UPF) to improve coverage, offload macro traffic, and support enterprise and private network scenarios.
VMR Phase 2 extends Rel-18 Vehicle Mounted Relays with additional ULI support and seamless operation over TN/NTN backhaul while remaining transparent to served UEs.
Rel-19 RAN topology cluster: 5G NR Femto, Additional Topological Enhancements for NR (5G_Femto / NR_WAB_5GFemto), and Vehicle Mounted Relays Phase 2 (VMR_Ph2).
Rel-19 continues NR MIMO evolution with further enhancements to multi-user MIMO, multi-TRP operation, CSI enhancements for AI/ML integration, and beam management refinements.
Rel-19 mobility enhancements including L1/L2-centric inter-cell mobility (LTM), multi-node information exchange, and necessary UE reporting for LTM. Built on Rel-18 mobility enhancements.

Rel-19 specifies Sub-Band Full Duplex in TDD systems: a portion of a downlink slot can be converted into an uplink sub-band orthogonal to the remaining downlink sub-bands, enabling simultaneous downlink and uplink in the same slot. Improves uplink coverage and reduces latency for TDD.

Rel-19 RAN cluster: NR MIMO Phase 5, NR Mobility Phase 4, Sub-Band Full Duplex (SBFD), sidelink enhancements, dual connectivity enhancements, NR/LTE band additions, HPUE, SON/MDT Phase 4, NR BS RF requirement evolution, NR RRM Phase 5, NR demodulation performance Phase 5, and ISAC channel modeling study.
Rel-19 enhancements of network slicing: AI/ML-based resource allocation for slices, slice-aware mobility, and tighter integration with the SBA for slice lifecycle management.
Rel-19 UPEAS Phase 2 extends the Service-Based Architecture to the UPF, enabling more service-based interactions for UPF exposure, traffic influence, and packet flow description handling.

description: Rel-19 enhancements of UE Policy (UEP19), Session Management Policy (SMPC19), and related QoS mechanisms.
Rel-19 multi-access enhancements for ATSSS (Access Traffic Steering, Switching, and Splitting) support over more access types and improved policy.

Rel-19 enhancements of Mission Critical Services (MCS) including MCPTT, MCVideo, MCData, eCall over IMS, and Emergency Services. Includes NG-RAN support for mission-critical push-to-talk over satellite.
Rel-19 UAS Phase 3: enhanced UAS connectivity, identification, tracking, and command-and-control via the 5G network, building on Rel-17/Rel-18 UAS work.

Rel-19 enhancements for Aerial UEs (UEs on aerial platforms such as drones). Includes uplink enhancements for aerial channel conditions, interference mitigation for aerial UEs, and support for high-altitude platforms.

Rel-19 ISAC channel modeling study: Integrated Sensing and Communication is one of the six IMT-2030 usage scenarios. The study identifies deployment scenarios for ISAC and defines channel models for sensing using existing 3GPP channel models as a starting point. Considers radar cross-section, mobility, clutter patterns, and spatial consistency.

Rel-19 7-24 GHz channel modeling study. 7.125-8.4 GHz and 14.8-15.35 GHz were agreed at WRC-23 as agenda items for WRC-27 and are likely 6G candidate frequencies. The work checks applicability of existing 5G channel models to 7-24 GHz and adds extensions for near-field effects and spatial non-stationarity that matter at higher frequencies with larger antenna arrays.

Rel-19 hosts two 6G bridge studies: ISAC channel modeling and 7-24 GHz channel modeling. Rel-19 is the last release fully dedicated to 5G; Rel-20 will start normative 6G studies, and Rel-21 (no earlier than March 2029) will produce the first 6G technical specifications for IMT-2030 submission before 2030.
Rel-19 sidelink enhancements including NR Sidelink Intra-band Carrier Aggregation in the ITS band, and continued evolution of ProSe and PC5 reference point.

Rel-19 enhancements for NR-DC (NR-NR Dual Connectivity), EN-DC (E-UTRA-NR Dual Connectivity), and MR-DC (Multi-Radio Dual Connectivity). AI/ML for mobility optimization in DC is part of AI/ML for NG-RAN enhancements.

Rel-19 Phase 3 of the Common API Framework (CAPIF), which defines how API invokers inside and outside the 3GPP system discover and consume 3GPP APIs. Includes support for additional API management features and tighter integration with NEF and the SCEF.
Rel-19 Phase 4 of Self-Organizing Networks and Minimization of Drive Tests, including support for SON/MDT in NTN scenarios and continuous MDT collection across RRC states for AI/ML training.

RAN-side Rel-19 work item that defines the physical-layer and protocol solutions for AmbientIoT devices in NR FR1 FDD spectrum. Two topologies: BS connected directly to a tag, or UE serving as an intermediate node. Both passive backscatter (around 1 microWatt) and active low-power transmission (a few hundred microWatts) are supported.
